source: YouTube auto-caption transcript 0:00-18:46 (tools/video_draft.py transcript VTU-DlQTMXA --start 0 --end 1125), card names corrected against data/Sets/FRA_PremierDraft_All_Data.json; nothing past 18:46 read. 'type' marks each idea as claim, heuristic or one-off pick; 'repeats' lists ideas of earlier videos it restates; 'related' lists looser topic matches.

ideas.claim: Ajani Unrelenting is completely busted: every loyalty activation (including his Jaces') makes a 2/2 Cadet, and the minus three deals four to each creature except his tokens, so it is a one-sided sweeper; he wants to build around it.
ideas.quote: But the real meat is the minus three. You deal four damage to each creature except for tokens you control.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Ajani Unrelenting; its win rate in decks with Jace-token makers.

ideas.claim: Ajani Resolute is cutesy in life-gain decks and really hard to get going; a two-mana planeswalker that is hard to use.
ideas.quote: This Ajani is kind of cutesy in life gain decks I think but it's kind of like it's really hard to use.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Ajani Resolute.

ideas.claim: Warrior's Blades is a card he likes but splashes into red or white decks rather than playing a red-white deck for it.
ideas.quote: I really like Warriors Blades, but I've kind of just been splashing it in my like red decks or white decks.
ideas.test_idea: Splash win rate of Warrior's Blades.

ideas.claim: Take more powerful cards early over the way-of-the-X enchantment: Your Fate Ends Here (hard removal with surveil) over Way of the Warlord and Yoshimaru, Scrappy Stray, which needs more setup.
ideas.quote: I would rather just take like a more powerful cards early on. And I think your fate ends here is a very powerful card.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Your Fate Ends Here against Yoshimaru, Scrappy Stray and Way of the Warlord.

ideas.claim: Four paired cards in a pack mean three pairs plus one standing in for a foil card, so a missing partner is weaker evidence than it looks.
ideas.quote: The reason there's four instead of three is because one of them represents like a foil card.
ideas.test_idea: How often a pack with four pair cards fits the three-pair-plus-foil structure.

ideas.claim: Gold-card pick at P1p3: Proctor of Potential (blue-white) over Mindseeker Oculus, abandoning the Ajani plan; later he calls it a misstep and says Oculus would have kept blue-red.
ideas.quote: Maybe a mis misstep with the Mindseker Oculus pick.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Proctor of Potential against Mindseeker Oculus; how often a P1p3 gold pick ends in the final deck.

ideas.claim: Passing Oculus costs a lot: he says 'my kingdom for the Oculus' twice as blue cards go by and the Oculus does not wheel; Oculus is one of his favourite cards.
ideas.quote: Oh, my kingdom for the Oculus. I've made a terrible mistake.
ideas.test_idea: Whether top-drafter win rate for Mindseeker Oculus decks beats alternatives at pick 3.

ideas.claim: Clash of Elements is a great removal spell and pulls him back to blue-red so that Ajani Unrelenting can be played.
ideas.quote: Clash of Elements. Very strong card, great removal spell.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Clash of Elements against other removal at pick 4.

ideas.claim: Way of the Pyromancer is worth trying with Ajani: a Jace taken up gives a 2/2 and mana; it also ramps towards the Ajani.
ideas.quote: Pretty cool with an Ajani let you like if you have a Jace you can take it up to get a two two get some mana.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Way of the Pyromancer; play rate at 2 copies.

ideas.claim: Good two-drops are not worth a high pick, but a random red two-drop (Eardrum Rattler) is taken over Tomik, Izzet Sparkmage because Tomik does not block; he hopes none of the cards in that pack make his deck.
ideas.quote: I'll just take a random two drop in red. Maybe set myself up a little bit.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Eardrum Rattler against Tomik, Izzet Sparkmage.

ideas.claim: Loyal Tutor can fetch the planeswalker (Ajani) but is not very good normally; he takes the Way of the Pyromancer instead.
ideas.quote: Loyal tutor. Search for a planeswalker card, reveal it and put it on top. I can go get my Ajani on... Interesting. Not very good normally.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Loyal Tutor.

ideas.claim: Unsummon works great in a tempo start and goes with a blue-red deck of planeswalkers and bounce; he later caps himself at two.
ideas.quote: Unsummon works great with this kind of tempo start that we have.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Unsummon with 1 and 2 copies.

ideas.claim: A card that survives your own sweeper has extra value: Tether Technician is taken over Afterthought Sentry because it survives the Ajani minus three.
ideas.quote: I'll take the technician. It survives through my Ajani, which is nice.
ideas.test_idea: Value of tokens and sweeper-proof creatures in Ajani Unrelenting decks.

ideas.claim: Garruk, Veiled Butcher is powerful enough to take over a blue-red pick and try red-black with a splash: 'such a messed up card'; he gives up Protege's Awakening and Unsummon for it.
ideas.quote: Garruk is like incredibly powerful. Like it's such a messed up card.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Garruk, Veiled Butcher; how often a P2p1 bomb outside the main colours ends in the deck.

ideas.claim: Violent Echoes is a really good kill spell that also empowers Jace.
ideas.quote: Violent Echoes really good kill spell that also empowers Jace.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Violent Echoes against other red removal.

ideas.claim: Plan for All Outcomes gives lots of empowering and combines with Way of the Pyromancer to reset a Jace token over and over.
ideas.quote: Plan for all outcomes. Gives me a lot of empowering. Goes well with like way of the pyromancer.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Plan for All Outcomes in decks with Way of the Pyromancer.

ideas.claim: Cap yourself at two Unsummons when the deck has card draw and empower Jace; two is fine.
ideas.quote: I think I would kind of cap myself at two unsummons, but I think two is fine.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of decks by Unsummon copies.

ideas.claim: A dual land that enters untapped with planeswalkers is worth taking over Heartstring Puller, since he will have many planeswalkers; Heartstring Puller is his second pick and Room of Refuge third.
ideas.quote: I'm going to have a lot of planeswalkers, so it'll come in untapped a lot of the time.
ideas.test_idea: Play rate of Innovative Commons in decks with planeswalkers; GIH WR of Heartstring Puller.

ideas.claim: Splash a white land in case he wants Proctor of Potential: he takes the Dedicated Commons over Sphinx's Approach, being pretty locked into red.
ideas.quote: Maybe I'll just take the white land in case I want to splash the proctor of potential or something.
ideas.test_idea: Whether dual lands taken for a splash card at pick 9 ever reach a deck.

ideas.claim: Opening two black mythics can jump you into a colour: Overwrite the Multiverse at P3p1 moves him back to black, splashing blue for one or two cards.
ideas.quote: Opening two black mythics can really jump you into a color, can't it?
ideas.test_idea: How often bombs taken in pack 3 change a drafter's colours; GIH WR of Overwrite the Multiverse.

ideas.claim: Winter, Tormented Loner is not good in a deck that wants to keep its planeswalkers and does little non-combat damage; he takes Extended Absence, which also improves Grim Repriser.
ideas.quote: we kind of want to keep our planeswalkers around. So, it's not as good in our deck.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Winter, Tormented Loner by colour pair; Grim Repriser with Extended Absence.

ideas.claim: A strong card in your colours before going 'too deep off the deep end': Pia, Determined Rebuilder over a land that would ease a blue splash, because the deck needs real playables.
ideas.quote: Let's just take the really good card for my deck in my colors before we go too deep off the deep end here.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Pia, Determined Rebuilder against splash-fixing lands.

ideas.claim: Splinter Twin combos with one blue card; he would have tried the combo if he had taken it earlier.
ideas.quote: Splinter Twin is super cool with like there's the one blue card that combos with it.
ideas.test_idea: Not testable on 17Lands data (a two-card combo); record only.

ideas.claim: Counting creatures during the draft: nine creatures is low, so he does not want a combat trick; he takes a creature at P3p8 and a kill spell at P3p9 because he already has five two-drops.
ideas.quote: My creature count seems low. Yeah, I have nine creatures, so I don't really want a combat trick.
ideas.test_idea: Creature count at pick 8 of pack 3 and final win rate.

ideas.claim: Wheeled Grim Repriser is not good in his deck: he has too few ways to ping the opponent, so he takes the land (Room of Refuge) so that he can play his cards.
ideas.quote: We don't have that many ways to ping them. So Heartstring puller might just be better.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Grim Repriser by number of ping sources.

ideas.claim: A blue splash of three cards (Plan for All Outcomes, Saheeli, Clash of Elements) with one Island is too light: three blue sources for three cards is not enough; he counts and settles on a few Islands.
ideas.quote: Four sources for three cards is not enough.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of three-card splashes by number of sources (3, 4, 5).

ideas.claim: Splash only three blue cards and play one Island plus dual lands: red and black have ten sources each, with 17 lands.
ideas.quote: So, this gives us five, six, seven, eight, nine, 10 red sources.
ideas.test_idea: Source counts (10 / 9 / 4) against win rate in two-base-colour decks with a light splash.

ideas.claim: He says twice that he does not really want Eardrum Rattler, yet it is still in the 40 at 18:46: the two-drop slot is kept for curve even though the card is the weakest.
ideas.quote: I don't really want eardrum rattler.
ideas.test_idea: Eardrum Rattler play rate and win rate.
